extracted.intended_audience: MathML authors, renderer implementers, authoring-tool developers, and web developers embedding MathML
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and normative recommendations from the MathML 4 specification covering embedding MathML in HTML, linking, graphical annotations, CSS interaction, character usage, validation, and best practices for authoring and rendering MathML.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use well-formed XML MathML fragments when embedding in HTML
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors and editing systems should use MathML fragments that are well formed XML, even when embedded in an HTML document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although applications accepting MathML in HTML documents must accept MathML making use of HTML parser features, they should offer a way to export MathML in a portable XML syntax. Failure to produce well-formed XML fragments can result in MathML being parsed as ordinary HTML and not rendered as MathML.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking: href usage and link targets
rubrics_metrics.description: In MathML, an element is designated as a link by the presence of the href attribute; the id attribute should be used to specify link targets and must be unique within the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MathML allows the href attribute on all elements, but most user agents cannot implement nested links or links on elements with no visible rendering; such links may have no effect. Presentation elements that do not ordinarily have a visual rendering (for example: mprescripts, malignmark, maligngroup) should not be used as linking elements. MathML-Core does not support href on all elements and introduces a specific 'a' element for linking — generators aiming for Core compatibility may restrict href use to 'a' or use a JavaScript polyfill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use semantics and annotation-xml for alternative graphical representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphical content (e.g., labeled diagrams) that supplements MathML expressions can be embedded via the semantics element using annotation-xml children (e.g., SVG, XHTML fragments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the MathML-Content representation as the first child of semantics (analogous to img's alt); this content is the best choice for non-visual rendering. Annotation-xml children may hold alternative representations (e.g., SVG or an XHTML img) that processors can choose for display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrict CSS properties that affect MathML layout
rubrics_metrics.description: Because MathML layout differs from the CSS visual formatting model, applications may choose to restrict CSS properties applicable to MathML to those that do not affect layout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A MathML renderer queries the style engine and uses returned values as input to its layout algorithms, but MathML does not mandate inheritance mechanisms. Stylesheets should be written so document-wide typographic changes do not alter the meaning of embedded MathML expressions. Do not rely on CSS to supply typographic information necessary for the proper understanding of an expression; expressions dependent on CSS for meaning will not be portable to non-CSS environments like computer algebra systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encode semantics-critical style in MathML attributes, use them as CSS selectors
rubrics_metrics.description: Use MathML mathematics style attributes (e.g., mathvariant, mathsize) as selectors for CSS rules so that style information necessary to the sense of an expression is encoded directly in MathML.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By using logical MathML attributes as selectors, authoring tools ensure that essential stylistic information remains with the markup and is not lost in non-CSS environments. Example: a stylesheet rule math *[mathsize='small'] { font-size: 80% } applies to children with mathsize='small'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of precedence for attributes vs style sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: When both element attributes and style sheets request changes to rendering properties, the order of processing must follow CSS cascading order, taking into account precedence of non-CSS presentational hints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MathML does not specify a processing mechanism; implementers should apply the usual CSS cascade rules and ensure non-CSS presentational hints (e.g., explicit MathML attributes) are taken into account with appropriate precedence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify/agree on characters for accents and stretchable accents
rubrics_metrics.description: The spec should specify which characters to use for mover/munder accents (e.g., hat, check, tilde, acute, grave, dot, ddot, breve, bar, vec), including stretchable options, so renderers and generators agree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a canonical set (or allowed set) of Unicode characters for each accent (examples: hat: '^', U+0302, U+02C6; vec: U+20D7, U+2192, U+27F6; bar/overline/underline options listed). This reduces guessing by authoring tools and improves interoperability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use mathvariant attribute for mathematical alphanumeric symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: MathML offers an alternative mechanism to specify mathematical alphanumeric characters via the mathvariant attribute on token elements (e.g., mi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A MathML processor must treat a mathematical alphanumeric character (when it appears) as identical to the corresponding combination of the unstyled character plus mathvariant. Renderers should distinguish combinations that have equivalent Unicode code points and may ignore combinations without assigned Unicode code points or lacking font support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat non-marking characters as meaningful for rendering and semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain non-marking characters (e.g., U+2061 FUNCTION APPLICATION, U+2062 INVISIBLE TIMES, U+2063 INVISIBLE SEPARATOR, U+2064 INVISIBLE PLUS) provide textual clues that improve print rendering, accessibility (audio), and semantic recovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use proper attributes on mo and mspace for page composition (like line-breaking). Recognize these non-marking characters' special roles instead of treating them as simple spacers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid keyboard-character substitutions; prefer precise Unicode math characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Keyboard characters frequently substitute for more appropriate mathematical Unicode characters (e.g., U+002D hyphen-minus for U+2212 minus sign). MathML renderers should treat keyboard characters as their mathematical equivalents in the appropriate context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat U+002D [HYPHEN-MINUS] as equivalent to U+2212 [MINUS SIGN] in formula contexts and as equivalent to U+2010 [HYPHEN] in mtext contexts. Encourage authoring tools to generate precise mathematical characters rather than relying on keyboard substitutes. For primes, encourage treating U+0027 [APOSTROPHE] as U+2032 [PRIME] where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer explicit script markup over pseudo-script characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Pseudo-script characters (primes, degree sign, etc.) should generally be encoded using explicit MathML script constructs (msup, msub, msubsup) rather than as literal pseudo-script characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit script markup prevents typesetting problems with stacked scripts (e.g., x' with subscript) and better reflects mathematical structure (e.g., (f+g)' should be encoded with an msup whose base is the entire expression). Authoring and validation tools are encouraged to generate recommended script markup. Pseudo-scripts may still be used in text contexts (mtext) for prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use combining characters for mathematical accents
rubrics_metrics.description: Combining Unicode characters intended for natural language accents should not be used to encode mathematical accents; use MathML script and overscript/underscript constructions instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combining characters may be used in multi-character identifiers or text when needed, but not as a substitute for mathematical markup. If a base character plus combining characters corresponds to a pre-composed character, treat it as that pre-composed character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validate MathML using the provided Relax NG schemas and normalize input first
rubrics_metrics.description: MathML documents should be validated with the Relax NG schema for MathML (XML encoding or compact notation). Some normalization (e.g., attribute-case and data-* handling) may be required before validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MathML-Core (and HTML-derived inputs) allows attributes like onclick without regard to case, but schema validation expects lowercase names; normalize attribute names to lowercase before validating. Any data-* attributes should be normalized/removed or the schema extended, because the provided sample schema only allows a fixed data-other attribute. Schemas for Core, Presentation, and MathML4 are available at the referenced URLs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect MathML-Core compatibility constraints (e.g., href support, attribute behavior)
rubrics_metrics.description: MathML-Core has different support for certain features (for example, it introduces a specific 'a' element rather than allowing href on all elements). Implementations and generators aiming for compatibility with MathML-Core should follow Core's constraints or provide polyfills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When targeting MathML-Core compatibility, restrict usage of attributes or elements (such as limiting href to the 'a' element) accordingly. Consult MathML-Core and the MathML4 schemas for specific attribute sets and behaviors.
